sources.citation: SPPEL (Scheme for Protection and Preservation of Endangered Languages, CIIL Mysuru). n.d. 'Eravallan Documentation' page (investigators V. Gnanasundaram, N. Vijayan, P. Suresh).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives location, names, 'unique aspects' (no gender in finite verbs, figurative marriage discourse, diglossic folklore), and the list of Gnanasundaram's publications; states that a sketch grammar 'encompassing Phonology, morphology, morpho-phonemics' was under preparation.

sources.citation: SPPEL. n.d. 'Eravallan Grammatical Features' (50 WALS-style features; source/investigators V. Gnanasundaram, N. Vijayan, P. Suresh).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress: 15 phonology features (14 consonants, 5 vowel qualities, syllable structure '(C)(C)(C)V(C)(C)(C)(C)', 'Tone: No tones', etc.); no stress/accent feature is included.

sources.citation: Gnanasundaram, V., N. Vijayan & P. Suresh. 2023. A Sketch Grammar of Eravalla. Mysuru: Central Institute of Indian Languages (SPPEL Grammatical Sketch series). 268 pp. ISBN 978-81-19411-32-0.

sources.note: The only full-length modern description; 268 pp. with a phonology chapter (SPPEL announced it as 'encompassing Phonology, morphology, morpho-phonemics'); the place a stress statement would be, superseding the 2012 monograph.

sources.citation: Gnanasundaram, Vadivelu. 2012. Study of Eravalla: linguistic, sociolinguistic and folkloristic aspects with comparative Eravalla-Tamil vocabulary. Coimbatore: Department of Linguistics, Bharathiar University. 172 pp. ISBN 9788191068262.

sources.note: Glottolog's sole descriptive reference (grammar sketch); ad hoc sketch grammar plus Eravalla-Tamil wordlist. An IJDL 2015 review says its phonology occupies only half a page, so a stress statement is unlikely but possible.
